assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, the active peptide forms) led directly to therapies that have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits emerging. Combines clear physiological discovery with very large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology and therapeutic translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's pharmaceutical development and other early proglucagon work (for example Habener, not on the credited list) complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Therapies are in wide use with large randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely and the underlying science is stable.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit between physiology, peptide identification and drug development is disputed
Whether an industrial drug-development contribution should be included alongside the basic discoveries

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells establish a new therapeutic modality, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; conceptually original and clinically transformative, with a growing extension to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T translation) and Sadelain (CAR design and costimulation) are central; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cell trials. Early chimeric receptor concepts (Eshhar and others) are outside the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved products since 2017 with multi-year follow-up; confirmation is strong, though long-term safety and solid-tumour efficacy remain open.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept is not on the credited list
Whether the prize should be anchored to the clinical translation or to receptor engineering

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling and a basic homeostatic principle, with wide relevance for secretory biology, metabolic disease, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily identified the Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) pathway, giving a clean and compact two-person configuration. Other contributors (for example Ron on the PERK/ATF4 arm) are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of confirmation across yeast and mammals; the principle is firmly established, while therapeutic payoff remains still developing.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation is limited so far
Other arms of the response (PERK, ATF6) may deserve recognition

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a rational and effective target in rheumatoid arthritis, which opened the era of biologic therapy across many inflammatory diseases. A clear, original, high-impact translational discovery.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive linked contributions (cytokine cascade concept and clinical proof of concept), which supports a coherent two-person prize. Wider contributions (for example the cA2/infliximab antibody development) are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of clinical use with extensive independent confirmation; recognition is mature and arguably overdue. I note my own field relation to rheumatology and weigh it by the same criteria as other fields.
uncertainties: Whether the antibody-engineering contributions deserve inclusion in the same prize
Overlap with the closely related IL-6 blockade candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway reveals how cytosolic DNA is sensed by innate immunity, with implications for infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies, lupus), cancer immunity and ageing; high conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP) and Barber (STING) are the most decisive credited contributors. Other credited names (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) were co-discoverers on specific steps, and some allocation remains contested.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is widely confirmed; clinical translation is still in early phases, so recognition may be somewhat premature but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Priority and allocation among the STING and cGAS discoverers
Therapeutic efficacy of pathway modulators is not yet established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition validated molecularly targeted cancer therapy and converted chronic myeloid leukemia into a largely manageable disease; a landmark in translational oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) fit a three-person configuration. Rowley and the BCR-ABL gene discoveries are outside the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data are abundant and confirmation is complete; however, the fundamental BCR-ABL discovery pre-dated the drug and may already be recognized by other prizes.
uncertainties: Industrial versus academic contribution to be weighed
Relation to earlier cancer genetics discoveries that are not credited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in disease now documented; major public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (VLP assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine concept and early development) are the central credited names; there is parallel work by others in vaccine development that complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data are strong and growing; the prize for the viral cause of cervical cancer was already awarded (2008), so this would be a complementary prevention prize.
uncertainties: Parallel priority claims in VLP vaccine development
Overlap with prior recognition of HPV in cervical cancer

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids opened a general method for growing self-renewing epithelial tissue from single cells, with applications to disease modelling, drug testing and personalized medicine.
assessment.attribution: Sato and Clevers provided the decisive intestinal organoid culture demonstration, giving a compact configuration; related stem cell and Lgr5 work by Clevers' group underpins it. Contributions in other organoid systems are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted in laboratories, but clinical impact is still developing and the tool nature of the discovery may favour waiting.
uncertainties: Whether the invention is better framed as a method or as a stem-cell biology discovery
